vetting_note: script type unresolved. Seen: Winterthur ASC 876, 54 IIIF leaves via iiif.quartexcollections.com (manifest a1c5092e-ccc6-4366-8cca-f993ddb54002, fetched with a Referer header, scratch only). Image 35 (p.31) carries about four lines of an unknown glyph script under blank staves; image 44 carries three lines of the same kind interleaved with staves and ending in a word in Latin letters; short monogram-like marks end hymns on images 34, 36, 39. So ciphertext of some kind survives, but it matches the Shaker 'spirit/unknown tongue' songs and gift writing (Andrews, The Gift to Be Simple; Winterthur notes another hymnal with songs in a spirit language) as well as a private substitution, and no key or study was found. status: Bierther, Briefe und Akten N.F. II/8 (1982), p. 405, a note near Nr. 238, read from Google Books snippets only: 'mit Schreiben Menzels, Hamburg, 23./13. Sept. 1633, präs. 22. Okt. (A. ebenda fol. 83-84, größtenteils in Chiffre, deren Auflösung jedoch fehlt; ein Resümee Richels in Geheimer Rat 195 Konv. ... Kschw 5988/3 fol. 15)'. The enclosure is a list of peace conditions that Bierther matches to the Dresden points. Richel's summary suggests the Munich court could read the letter in 1633. Not the same as lead 2183, though that letter is dated the day this one arrived.
why: A mostly enciphered report from Hamburg to Maximilian on peace terms in 1633. The editor found no decipherment with it, but a contemporary summary survives as a check on any reading.
